agent: member-signatures (signature wave: CMoveCommand, CInGameIdler, CWar, CUndeclaredWar, and four singles)
question: Give the last of the unsigned member functions a signature: return type, calling convention, parameters, and above all the receiver, read off the ret and the call sites.

addresses.name: CMoveCommand::CMoveCommand_default
addresses.comment: CMoveCommand constructor that leaves every field zero. **The object arrives on the stack, not in ecx**: `mov esi,[ebp+8]` at 0x1D870D is the only thing it takes, ecx is never read, and it gives the object back in eax and does `ret 4`. Writes CCommand's table (0x15B4F74) first and CMoveCommand's own (0x15C8C1C) at 0x1D8770, sets the type id 0x18D at +4 and 0x255 at +0x2C/+0x30, empties the strings at +8 and +0x48, and zeroes +0x64..+0x6A.
addresses.revises: the entry recorded no signature at all; the receiver is a stack argument, which is why it needed one
addresses.evidence: `ret 4` at 0x1D87E8 against a body whose only argument reference is `mov esi,[ebp+8]`; ecx is dead on entry (no read before it is overwritten at 0x1D8710). Its one caller, 0x886FB3, does `push eax; call` after allocating 0x70 bytes and sets no ecx. Shown wrong by: any read of ecx before 0x1D8710, or a caller that loads ecx for it - there is exactly one caller, so that is cheap to re-check.

addresses.name: CMoveCommand::CMoveCommand
addresses.signature: CMoveCommand* __stdcall CMoveCommand::CMoveCommand(CMoveCommand* out, int targetProvince, bool mode68, bool safe, bool verySafe, CUnit* unit@EDI)
addresses.comment: CMoveCommand constructor, `ret 0x14`. The object is the **first stack argument** (`mov esi,[ebp+8]`), returned in eax; the four values go to +0x64 (target province), +0x68 (mode68), +0x69 (safe) and +0x6A (very safe). **The unit arrives in edi**, unset anywhere in the body: it is pushed with `lea edx,[esi+0x3C]` into 0x42DD70, which builds the command's object reference from it, and then `[edi+0x130]`'s +0xD0 - the unit's current province - is stored at +0x6C.
addresses.revises: the entry recorded no signature; the object is on the stack and the unit is a register argument, neither of which was written down
addresses.evidence: `ret 0x14` = five stack dwords, and every one of +8, +0xC, +0x10, +0x14, +0x18 is read. edi is pushed at 0x1D885E and read at 0x1D8893 with no write to it in the function, so it comes in; the call site at 0x5B9E58 sets it explicitly (`mov edi,esi`, esi being the unit whose +0x130 it had just read) and the one at 0x89A9DF has edi = the unit from [ebp+8] of CMoveCommand::IssueFromInterface. Constructor check: it writes 0x15C8C1C, CMoveCommand's own table. Shown wrong by: a call site that leaves edi holding something that is not a unit, or a use of edi in the body before 0x1D885E.

addresses.name: CMoveCommand::RouteUnit
addresses.comment: CMoveCommand vftable slot 6: works the unit's route out with one of three finders and gives it to the unit. Ordinary __thiscall - the command is in ecx (`mov esi,ecx` at 0x1D88E0, then +0x40/+0x44, the object reference pair) and it takes nothing on the stack (bare `ret`). Nothing is returned: eax at the exit is the leftover of the list-freeing loop at 0x1D9120.
addresses.revises: the entry recorded no signature; slot 6 is a plain __thiscall with no arguments, which the ret proves
addresses.evidence: A cfg walk of the whole 615-instruction body finds one `ret` immediate, 0 - so nothing is cleaned and there are no stack arguments; ecx is taken into esi in the second instruction. vtable.py --holding: CMoveCommand slot 6 and no other table. Shown wrong by: a `ret N` on a path the walk did not reach, or a read of [ebp+8] in the body.

addresses.name: CMoveCommand::CMoveCommand_copy
addresses.comment: CMoveCommand copy body, `ret 4`. **The receiver is the source, not the destination**: ecx is the command being copied (`mov edi,ecx`, then every read is [edi+...]) and the new object is the stack argument (`mov esi,[ebp+8]`, every write is [esi+...], and it is returned in eax). It writes CMoveCommand's table into the new object, then copies +0x3C/+0x40/+0x44 (the object reference), the string at +0x48, +0x64 and the routing bytes +0x68/+0x69/+0x6A and +0x6C. Called from exactly one place, 0x1D93BB, inside CMoveCommand slot 13 (0x1D9380) - the clone - which allocates 0x70 bytes and passes them in.
addresses.revises: the entry recorded no signature, and the direction was not written down: an MSVC copy constructor has the destination in ecx, and this one has the source
addresses.evidence: The vftable write `mov dword ptr [esi], 0x15C8C1C` at 0x1D941A lands on the stack argument, and an object gets its table when it is being built, so esi is the new one; all the `mov reg,[edi+...]` reads are from ecx. The single call site at 0x1D93B8 is `push eax` (a fresh 0x70-byte allocation) with `mov ecx,esi` (the existing command). `ret 4` for one stack dword. Shown wrong by: a second caller that passes them the other way round, or the 0x70 allocation turning out not to be a CMoveCommand.

addresses.name: CMoveCommand::IssueFromInterface
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CMoveCommand::IssueFromInterface(void* issuer@ECX, CUnit* unit, int provinceId, int recordOnly, bool safe, bool verySafe, int unused)
addresses.comment: What the GUI calls to issue a move; hardcodes mode68 = 1 and forwards its fourth and fifth arguments as safe and very safe; `ret 0x18`. The unit is the first stack argument (+0x158 gate, virtual +0x8C asked whether the province is reachable); `provinceId` indexes the game state's province vector at +0xB8C; when `recordOnly` is greater than zero it only writes the province to the unit's +0x2CC and returns; the sixth stack dword is never read on any path. **The receiver in ecx is not a CMoveCommand** - it is only ever handed on, as the first argument of 0x49ABD0 (issue a command of type id, 0x18D here or 0x5A4 for the sibling path) and of 0x499E50, which does `add ecx,0x20; call 0x402610`, so the object carries a CCountryTag at +0x20: the per-player interface the order is issued through. Its class was not identified.
addresses.revises: the entry recorded no signature; the six stack arguments and the register receiver are what it needed, and the receiver is left void* rather than guessed
addresses.evidence: `ret 0x18` = six stack dwords; +8, +0xC, +0x10, +0x14 and +0x18 are all read and a scan of the whole 188-instruction body finds no reference to [ebp+0x1C]. ecx is saved to [ebp-0x10] at 0x49A865 and passed on at 0x49A93B, 0x49A98C and 0x49A9A1. 0x499E50 treating its +0x20 as a CCountryTag is the one positive fact about it: 0x402610 reads [ecx] and [ecx+4] and indexes the country array at g_1A855A4+0x16C. **This entry will show up under checkSignatures' 'member functions whose signature never mentions their class'** - correctly, because the receiver is not a CMoveCommand and writing one in would be an invention. Shown wrong by: identifying the ecx class (then the signature should name it), or a caller that leaves the sixth argument meaningful.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::Update
addresses.comment: Per-frame update of the in game idler, virtual slot 1; calls the autosave writer (0x24FF80, `push ebx` with ebx = this, at 0x255E28). `ret 4`, but **no implementation of slot 1 reads its stack argument** - not this one, not CEU3Idler's at 0x244750, not CFrontEnd's at 0x2EDD60 (which only forwards it to the base), not CBackEndIdler's 0x208AF0 or CNudgeIdler's 0x29BE90 - so the argument is real but its meaning is not recoverable from the bodies. Frame timing is taken from the clock at +0x192C instead, into +0xA88/+0xA8C.
addresses.revises: the entry recorded no signature; slot 1 takes one stack dword, which the ret fixes even though nothing reads it
addresses.evidence: `ret 4` on every path of the 1178-instruction walk, and a scan of that walk for [ebp+8] finds nothing; the same scan on the other four implementations of the slot finds only CFrontEnd's pass-through at 0x2EDD74. vtable.py --holding: CInGameIdler slot 1 alone. Shown wrong by: a slot-1 call site that clearly pushes a float or a pointer, which would name the argument.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::DailyUpdate
addresses.comment: CInGameIdler virtual slot 53: repaints the map in modes 4/18/19, then always runs the autosave check. Takes nothing on the stack (bare `ret` on all three paths) and returns true - every path sets `al, 1` before the epilogue. The mode is the dword at +0xD34; mode 4 calls MapMode_Supply_Colour (0x266EE0), 0x12 and 0x13 go through 0x46A1E0/0x46AD60 and 0x46A6F0 on the map object's +0x1DC4; every path ends with `push esi; call 0x261D20`, the autosave check.
addresses.revises: the entry recorded no signature; it is a no-argument __thiscall that returns a bool, and the bool was not recorded
addresses.evidence: Three `ret` instructions, all bare, at 0x261CC7/0x261CF3/0x261D18, each preceded by `mov al, 1`; ecx into esi at 0x261CA7. vtable.py --holding: CInGameIdler slot 53 alone. Shown wrong by: a caller that ignores al on a slot where other classes return something else - the return was read off this body only.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::AutosaveWrite
addresses.comment: Writes the autosave when idler +0xAB0 is set, after one frame of delay; builds the file name from debug_saves. **The idler is a stack argument, not ecx** (`mov esi,[ebp+8]`), matching the neighbouring AutosaveCheck (0x261D20), which is recorded the same way. `ret 4`, no return value: on the first frame it just sets +0xAB1 and leaves. Not a virtual, and called from exactly one place, 0x255E28 in CInGameIdler::Update.
addresses.revises: the entry recorded no signature; it is __stdcall on a stack receiver rather than the __thiscall its name suggests
addresses.evidence: `mov esi,[ebp+8]` at 0x24FFA0 then [esi+0xAB0]/[esi+0xAB1], the autosave request pair; both exits `ret 4`; the one call site is `push ebx; call 0x24FF80` with ebx the idler that Update took from ecx. Shown wrong by: any read of ecx in the body - there is none before it is used as scratch.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::SetAutosaveRequested
addresses.comment: Virtual setter (slot 92) for the autosave request pair; clears +0xAB1 whenever +0xAB0 is set to 0. Nine instructions: `mov al,[ebp+8]; mov [ecx+0xAB0],al; test al,al; jne; mov [ecx+0xAB1],al`, then `ret 4`. The byte it leaves in al is the argument, not a return value.
addresses.revises: the entry recorded no signature; this is the plainest __thiscall in the set and had none
addresses.evidence: The whole body is visible at 0x275090..0x2750A7: ecx is the object, [ebp+8] the byte, `ret 4`. vtable.py --holding: CInGameIdler slot 92 alone. Shown wrong by: a caller that reads eax afterwards, which would make the al a return.

addresses.name: CWar::AddAttacker
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CWar::AddAttacker(CWar* war, bool arg2, bool arg3, char tag[4], int countryId)
addresses.comment: Adds a country to a war's attackers, the vector at +0x2C. The loader calls it for every `attacker=` line, after refusing a tag the country database does not know. **Everything is on the stack** (`mov esi,[ebp+8]`, `ret 0x14`) and the last two dwords are one `CCountryTag` passed by value - char[4] then id - spelled out as two parameters here so the arithmetic checks: the id at [ebp+0x18] is what the search over the existing 8-byte entries compares, and `lea ecx,[ebp+0x14]; call 0x402610` resolves the pair to a CCountry. The two flags are bytes: [ebp+0x10] (arg3) is cleared when the first existing attacker's country has a zero byte at +0xF34 and, once zero, skips the bulk of the function; [ebp+0xC] (arg2) is tested near the end. What the two mean was not settled - across the call sites arg2 is 1 or 0 and arg3 is 0 or a zeroed register at every one of them.
addresses.revises: the entry recorded the argument list in prose and no signature; this fixes the convention and says the last two dwords are one CCountryTag by value
addresses.evidence: `ret 0x14` = five stack dwords, all five read; CWar +0x2C/+0x30 are attackers/attackers_end in project.json and the walk over `[eax+4] == [ebp+0x18]` in 8-byte steps is a CCountryTag vector search. 0x402610 is the tag-to-country lookup ([ecx] chars discarded, [ecx+4] indexing g_1A855A4+0x16C), which fixes which half is the id. Call sites 0x4BEB59, 0x6009DC, 0xA125ED, 0xA12641, 0xA129EA, 0xA12AFF, 0xA16E2F, 0xA288F5 and 0xA4E8D9 all push five. Shown wrong by: naming the two flags, or a call site that passes something other than a GetTag result as the last pair.

addresses.name: CWar::AddDefender
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CWar::AddDefender(CWar* war, bool arg2, bool arg3, char tag[4], int countryId)
addresses.comment: The same for the defenders, the vector at +0x3C: the same five stack arguments, the same `ret 0x14`, the same CCountryTag pair at the end and the same pair of flags. The only difference in the first thirty instructions is `add edi, 0x3C` where the attacker side has +0x2C.
addresses.revises: the entry recorded no signature; it mirrors AddAttacker and now says so
addresses.evidence: `ret 0x14`, `mov edi,[ebp+8]` then [edi+0x3C]/[edi+0x40] - defenders/defenders_end in project.json - and the same 8-byte search against [ebp+0x18]. Call sites 0x4BEB69 and 0xA12AE6 push five, in the same order as the attacker calls beside them. Shown wrong by: the same things as AddAttacker.

addresses.name: CUndeclaredWar::AddAttacker
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CUndeclaredWar::AddAttacker(CUndeclaredWar* war, char tag[4], int countryId)
addresses.comment: Adds a country to an undeclared war's attackers, the vector at +0x8. Three stack dwords, `ret 0xC`: the war, then one `CCountryTag` by value, spelled as its two halves. It appends the tag (`lea edi,[ebx+8]`, the pair's address in eax, 0x22690) and then walks the **defenders** at +0x18, setting each `countries[thisId]->+0xE28[thatId]->+0x24` and the mirror to the war - the pairwise relation both ways round.
addresses.revises: the entry recorded no signature; it is __stdcall with the war on the stack and takes a CCountryTag by value
addresses.evidence: `ret 0xC`; `mov ebx,[ebp+8]` with +8/+0xC and +0x18/+0x1C being attackers/defenders in project.json; [ebp+0x10] is used as the country index (`[edx + ecx*4]` into g_1A855A4+0x16C) and [ebp+0xC] only as the first half of the 8-byte element, which is CCountryTag's char[4]. Caller 0x9BCFBD pushes [arg+0x14], [arg+0x10] and the war; caller 0x475D75 pushes the two dwords of the CCountryTag that CCountryDataBase::GetTag (0x118480) had just filled at [esp+0x14]. Shown wrong by: the element at +8 turning out to be wider than 8 bytes, which the `add eax,8` stride refutes.

addresses.name: CUndeclaredWar::AddDefender
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CUndeclaredWar::AddDefender(CUndeclaredWar* war, char tag[4], int countryId)
addresses.comment: The same for the defenders, at +0x18: it appends to +0x18 and walks the attackers at +0x8. Instruction for instruction the mirror of AddAttacker, `ret 0xC`.
addresses.evidence: `ret 0xC`; `lea edi,[ebx+0x18]` before the append at 0x4761D5 where the attacker side has +8, and the loop bound is [ebx+8]/[ebx+0xC]. Callers 0x475C35 and 0x9BCFCD push three, the same shape as the attacker calls next to them. Shown wrong by: the same things as AddAttacker.

addresses.name: CCombatHistoryEntry::CCombatHistoryEntry
addresses.signature: CCombatHistoryEntry* __stdcall CCombatHistoryEntry::CCombatHistoryEntry(CCombatHistoryEntry* this@ESI, CCombat* combat@ECX, int* tick@EAX)
addresses.comment: CCombatHistoryEntry constructor; fills the entry from a CCombat (tick, kind, winner tag, flag, province). **It takes nothing on the stack at all** - bare `ret` - and all three arguments are registers: the entry in esi (written throughout, returned in eax), the combat in ecx, and a pointer to the tick in eax, whose target goes to +8. It writes its own vftable 0x15B68C0 and the 0x18D at +4, takes the kind from the combat's virtual slot 0x2C, the flag from the combat's byte +0x2B, the province from [combat+0x18]'s +0xD0, and the two CCountryTags at +0x10 and +0x18 from the combat's +0x10 and +0x14 sides - writing the literal `---` (three `mov` of 0x2D and a NUL) with id 0 where a side has none.
addresses.revises: the entry recorded no signature; three register arguments and no stack at all is exactly the case the findings notation exists for
addresses.evidence: Bare `ret` on both exits and no [ebp+...] argument read; esi is never written before its first use, nor is eax before `mov ecx,[eax]` at 0x2F357, nor ecx before `mov edi,ecx`. The one call site, 0x2F9FE inside RecordCombat, sets all three: `mov ecx,[ebp+0xC]` (the combat), `add eax,0xBDC` on the game state - CCurrentGameState +0xBDC is `tick` in project.json - and `lea esi,[ebp-0x38]`, a stack temporary. The `---` writes match CCountryTag's documented no-country value. Shown wrong by: a second caller setting the registers differently, or +0xBDC turning out not to be the tick.

addresses.name: CCombatHistory::RecordCombat
addresses.comment: Appends an entry to the combat history when a combat ends; arg1 the list, arg2 the finished CCombat. Hooked at its first instruction. Both arguments are on the stack and it cleans them (`ret 8` on both exits); nothing is returned. It builds the entry in a stack temporary through CCombatHistoryEntry::CCombatHistoryEntry - passing the game state's tick pointer in eax and the combat in ecx - then allocates 0x34 bytes and copies the temporary into the list held at the history's +0xC.
addresses.revises: the entry recorded no signature; the __stdcall pair on the stack is what the hook has to be written against
addresses.evidence: `ret 8` on both exits; `mov eax,[ebp+8]` then [eax+0xC] (CCombatHistory last_entry in project.json) and `mov ecx,[ebp+0xC]` straight into the entry constructor as the combat. Shown wrong by: a caller that leaves something in a register the body reads - none is read before being written here.

addresses.name: CTraitGainTracker::SaveContents
addresses.comment: Walks the map at `+0xC` - a red-black tree, the value at each node's `+0x10` - and writes one key per trait. That this class has a SaveContents of its own, rather than the shared empty one at `0x20CD50`, is what says the progress is game state rather than a definition. **Read live**: a leader's history holds the tracker, at `CLeaderHistory + 0x40` - 399 of 400 histories in a running game point at one. It is virtual slot 2, the CPersistent save hook, with the ordinary shape of one: tracker in ecx, writer on the stack, `ret 4`.
addresses.revises: the entry recorded no signature; it has the same shape as CCountry::SaveContents, which is signed, and now says so
addresses.evidence: `ret 4`; `mov ebx,[ecx+0xC]` and `mov [ebp-4],ecx` at the top, `mov edi,[ebp+8]` for the writer. vtable.py --holding: CTraitGainTracker slot 2 and no other table, and no direct callers - it is only ever reached through the slot. Shown wrong by: the argument turning out to be something other than a CSaveWriter, which the slot's other implementations settle.

addresses.name: CBrigadeConstructionDefinition::SetName
addresses.comment: Assigns the brigade's name at +0x18 (`lea ecx,[edi+0x18]`, std::string::assign with 0 and -1) and then hands the owning country and that same string to 0xCB450. Both arguments are registers and it takes nothing on the stack - no frame beyond `push ecx` for one local, and a bare `ret`; the caller at 0x82E4D sets `esi` from std::string::fromCString and `edi` from the object. **The lookup is a country lookup, not a string one**: `lea ecx,[edi+8]; call 0x402610` reads +8 and +0xC as a CCountryTag and returns `countries[id]`. project.json records +0x8 as `display_name Hoi3CString`, which cannot be right - a Hoi3CString is 0x18 bytes, so one at +8 would swallow +0x10, +0x14 and the name at +0x18. The field was left alone here rather than renamed on the strength of one call site.
addresses.revises: the entry recorded no signature and described +8 as a second string; the convention is two register arguments, and what happens to +8 is a country lookup
addresses.evidence: Bare `ret` and no [ebp+...] at all (there is no ebp frame); edi and esi are read before any write. The stack accounting balances only if 0xCB450 is __stdcall with two arguments, which it is (`ret 8`). 0x402610's body is unambiguous: [ecx] discarded, [ecx+4] used as [g_1A855A4+0x16C][id]. Shown wrong by: the object in edi turning out not to be a CBrigadeConstructionDefinition - the name is inherited, not re-derived here - or +8 being shown to be a string by the class's own loader.

slots_noted: Only the five addresses that sit in a table are recorded above; the other twelve are in none (vtable.py --holding). CInGameIdler slots 1, 53 and 92 are its own overrides - the bodies appear in no other class's table - so no sibling or base record follows from them, and CMoveCommand slot 6 was already recorded and is repeated unchanged.
